Mahbubur Rahman with Farah Mahbub, Anisur Rahman Patwari, Advocates -----For the Petitioner.
KS Nabi, Attorney-General with Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Additional Attorney-General, Serajul Huq, Special PP, M Faruque, Deputy Attorney-General, MA Rouf, Assistant Attorney-General------For the State.
parties:
Jobaida Rashid ----- Petitioner
Vs
State, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Badrul Islam Choudhury J: Rule was issued on petition under section 439 read with section 435 CrPC upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka representing the State, to show cause as to why the order dated 7-4-97 passed by the Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Sessions Case No. 319 of 1997 framing charge against the petitioner Mrs. Jobaida Rashid should not be set aside. By order of the same date further proceedings of the above mentioned Sessions Case was stayed. 

 AFM Mahitul Islam receptionist-cum-residence PA of the then President of the Republic of Bangladesh Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, on 2-10-96 filed a written First Information Report at Dhanmondi PS alleging, inter alia, that in the night following 14th August 1975 he was on duty at the residence of the then President Sheikh Mujibur Rahman situated at No. 677 of Road No. 32, Dhanmondi Residential Area. In the First Information Report he gave a detailed description of the occurrence as to how the then President, his wife, some members of his family and some officials on duty were killed by the army personnel in the early hours of 15-8-75. In the First Information Report 14 persons including the husband of present petitioner Major Khandker Abdur Rashid, all of whom were army officers, and some others were named as the persons who committed the offence. On receipt of the said First Information Report Dhanmondi Police started case No. 10(10)96 dated 2-10-96 and took up investigation. 

 3. In the present petition under consideration, it has been stated that on 14-8-96 and 12-10-96 police and other personnel of investigating agencies including the CID encircled the residence of the petitioner at No. 7 Gulshan, Road No. 55 and entered into the premises in search of the First Information Report named accused Major Khandker Abdur Rashid (who subsequently was promoted to the post of Lieutenant Colonel wherefrom he retired.). It is contended further that the petitioner wanted to see the search warrant but the personnel of law enforcing agencies failed to show any search warrant but forcibly entered into the house creating an atmosphere of terror and panic. Members of the law enforcing agencies again raided the house of the petitioner and conducted search on 14-10-96, 25-10-96 and 2-11-96. On those days the petitioner along with her unmarried daughters were residing in the house. That police made unauthorised search without any warrant in the house at night and there were altercations and exchange of hot words between the petitioner and police officers including those of the CID and on every occasion they threatened the petitioner to teach a good lesson which, according to them, she would never forget in life. On 12-10-96 on search the law enforcing agencies seized one licensed pistol belonging to the petitioner from her bedroom and a revolver and a shotgun from the bedroom of her husband which were also held under valid licence. The licences were also seized and Gulshan PS case No. 9 (11)96 dated 2-11-96 was started under the Arms Act, though the seizing authority gave a certificate on 14-8-96 after search, that they did not find anything seizable in the house. It is further stated that during the repeated search the house was ransacked and altercations took place between the petitioner on the one hand and the police and CID personnel on the other, when she was forced to sign the seizure list as there was nothing illegal or unlicensed found in the house. Subsequently it transpired to the petitioner that with ulterior motive the police and CID personnel made fraudulent and incorrect seizure list showing extra ammunition which they might have planted or placed in her house. In that situation the petitioner held a press conference on 25-10-96 in which she informed the assembled newsmen about the atrocities of the law enforcing agencies inflicted on her and members of her family and also proposed to hold another press conference on 3-11-96. That during the second round of altercation the aforesaid police officials became furious and they said that though they-came to search the house in connection with Gulshan PS case No. 9(11)96 under the Arms Act but now the petitioner would have to face music in connection with Dhanmondi PS case No. 10(10)96 and asked her to go to Gulshan PS at that hour of night, though there was no warrant of arrest with respect to the petitioner. She was forcibly taken to Gulshan PS where she was detained for the whole night and the following day in an unhealthy and unbearable condition and then she was produced before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Dhaka in the afternoon of 3-11-96 showing her arrested in connection with the arm case being Gulshan PS case No. 9(11)96. On the prayer of the police the CMM granted 5 days police remand during which the petitioner was unbearably, physically and mentally tortured in an uncivilised and brutal manner due to which she was taken to Rajarbag police hospital. At the end of the remand period she was again produced before the CMM and a bail petition was moved on behalf of the petitioner. The learned CMM rejected the bail petition and ordered for sending her to judicial custody (hajat). But the CID which took up investigation of both the cases made a prayer for showing her arrested in connection with Dhanmondi PS case No.10(10)96 and also prayed for 4 days' police remand. The CMM allowed both the prayers and the CID took her into their custody. It is alleged in the petition that during this remand period the petitioner was again subjected to shocking, shameful, and unbearable torture, both physical and mental and that she was told that until she agreed to sign confessional statement in connection with the aforementioned Dhanmondi PS case torture on her and also on her two unmarried daughters would be intensified and prolonged. She was also given the allurement that she would be released to go to her house with her two daughters if she confessed. It is further alleged that trained dogs were used to torture her and she was kept blindfolded on the floor, water was poured on her head, she was given electrical shock and was not allowed to drink water when she was thirsty, she was not allowed to respond to the call of nature or use the toilet. Under these situations she was taken to the court of a Magistrate who took her signature on a statement which was not made by her. The signature was given in the statement, involuntarily, under duress, coercion, pressure, torture and inducement which in no way was voluntary or true. That when she was taken to the court of Magistrate she was escorted by police and the Investigating officer of the case who remained present all along in the court premises within the sight of the petitioner and, as such, the confessional statement was liable to be retracted and cancelled. After obtaining her signatures on the alleged confessional statement she was sent to Dhaka Central Jail, that in spite of her prayer she was refused bail as well as Division in the jail by the CMM by order dated 28-11-96. She was also refused the privilege of consulting her lawyers. There was also separate petition for producing her before the CMM for the purpose of retracting her confession and the CMM ordered that she could send the retraction petition through jail authority, but the CMM ordered for giving her proper treatment and medicine which was also denied by the jail authority. However, on a prayer made, the Sessions Judge, Dhaka ordered for her Division in the jail and the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.552/97 granted her bail. Police submitted charge sheet against 20 persons including the present petitioner out of whom 14 were shown absconding, six in custody including the petitioner and subsequently the petitioner was enlarged on bail by the High Court Division. The learned Sessions Judge on receiving the case record fixed 7-4-97 for framing of charge. There was a petition on the side of the petitioner for discharging her under section 265C CrPC but the Sessions Judge rejected that prayer and framed charges under sections 120B, 302/34 and 201 of the Penal Code against all the accused persons including the present petitioner. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of the Sessions Judge dated 7-4-97 framing charge against her the High Court Division was moved with present revisional application under sections 439/435 CrPC and the Rule obtained. 

 6. Heard Mr. Mahbubur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused petitioner, Mr KS Nabi, the learned Attorney-General and Mr. Serajul Huq who being appointed Special Public Prosecutor for the purpose of conducting the sessions case also appeared and made submissions. Mr. Rahman has taken us through the Annexures filed with the petition which include petition for granting bail and the order of the CMM sending the petitioner to hajat after 5 days' police remand and the CID's prayer for showing her arrested in connection with Dhanmondi PS case No. 10(10)96 and also for police remand. We have also gone through the petitions seeking direction to produce the petitioner in court of the CMM for retracting the confessional statement made on 20-2-97 and the CMM's order in this regard directing that the retraction petition could be sent through Jail authority, that the DIG Prisons, should take step for giving her Division and his refusal to grant bail. But these are matters with which we are not directly concerned in the present revisional application. We are to see whether there were sufficient materials before the Sessions Judge to frame charge against the accused petitioner Mrs. Jobaida Rashid under sections 120B, 302/34 and 201 of the Penal Code or whether she ought to have been discharged for lack of sufficient materials. 

 8. Mr Serajul Huq during his brief, but to the point argument has referred to sections 10 and 30 of the Evidence Act and has contended that in a case of criminal conspiracy the evidence due to the very nature of the offence alleged, is bound to be referential and not direct and in the instant case, as per Mr Huq, since the petitioner was found very active at Bangabhaban on 15th August, 1975 during the oath taking ceremony of Khandker Mostaque Ahmed as the President on that very day, and statements of some witnesses, it can safely be presumed that the petitioner Jobaida Rashid was very much involved in the conspiracy along with other accused persons of the case who committed the murder of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. 

 9. Mr. Serajul Huq's contention is that' three of the 74 witnesses examined in this case under section161 CrPC and two other charge-sheeted accused persons in their confession made reference about the involvement of the petitioner in the conspiracy and, as such, the statement of those witnesses and the confessional statements of the two accused persons may be taken into consideration at the time of trial and, as such, there were sufficient materials before the Sessions Judge to frame charge against the petitioner. 

 10. On the other hand, in the case of Queen vs. Blake 1844, 6 QB 126, it was observed: 

 "The words written or spoken may be a declaration accompanying an act and indicating the quality of the act as being an act in the course of the conspiracy or the words written or spoken may in themselves be acts done in the course of the conspiracy. This being the principle, their Lordships think the words of section 10 must be construed in accordance with it and are not capable of being widely construed so as to include a statement made by one conspirator in the absence of the other with reference to the past acts, done in the actual course of carrying out the conspiracy after it has been completed. But it would be a very difficult matter to hold that any narrative or statement or confession made to a third party after the common intention or conspiracy was no longer operating and had caseed to exist is admissible against the other party. There is then no common intention of the conspirators to which the statement can have reference." 

 11. In the instant case there is no dispute about the fact that the materials which the investigating agencies have collected against the petitioner before us are (i) a retracted confessional statement made by the petitioner herself (ii) the so-called extra judicial confessional statement made by co-accused Lieutenant Colonel Abdur Rashid, the husband of the petitioner before a witness, namely Major General (Retired) Khalilur Rahman at Bangabhaban on 15th August 1975 "after the common intention or conspiracy was no longer operating" (iii) the confessional statements of Lieutenant Colonel Sultan Shariar Rashid Khan and Lieutenant Colonel (Retired) Syed Faruque Rahman recorded by the Magistrate under section 164 CrPC and (iv) the statement of 3 witnesses, namely, Major General (Retired) Safiullah, Major General (Retired) Khalilur Rahman and Air Vice Marshal (Retired) AK Khandker recorded under section 161 CrPC by the Investigating Officer. 

 13. In the case of Khondker Maniruzzaman vs. State reported in 17 BLD (1997) 11, a Division Bench of this court has held: "After repeal of old chapter XVIII of the Code of Criminal Procedure section 265C and 265D have been inserted in chapter XXIII of the Code of Criminal Procedure with positive object to enquire and look into so that innocent persons may not be harassed on false and vexatious allegations. Section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure reads as follows: 

 "265C. If, upon consideration of the case and the documents submitted therewith, and after hearing the submissions of the accused and the prosecution in this behalf, the court considers that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused it shall discharge the accused and record the reasons for so doing." 

 Now the law is settled by our judicial pronouncement of this court that this court under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure having supervisory jurisdiction can scrutinise and go into facts to examine the propriety of the impugned order passed under section 265C or 265D of the Code. In the case of AKM Mohinus Saleh and others vs. State, reported in 45 DLR 386 it has been held: 

 "From the statements of the witnesses it appears that on the day of occurrence the respondent was in the office and further from the office room of the respondent Chinese axe and other deadly weapons were brought out by several accused persons. Primarily on the basis of these broad statements charge was framed against the respondent under sections 302/109 and 307/109 of the Penal Code. The learned Judges of the High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record found that there was no sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused respondent on the charge of abetment for murder or for attempt to murder and consequently discharged the accused from the Sessions Case. Thus it appears that the Additional Sessions Judge without proper consideration of the materials on record and application of mind to section 265C and 265D of the Code wrongly opined that there is ground for presuming that the respondent had committed the offence of abetment and wrongly framed charge against him when, as a matter of factabe materials on record do not sufficiently provide any ground that the accused is involved as an abettor in the offence as alleged." 

 For proper appreciation of this decision of the Appellate Division we would like to narrate briefly, the facts of that case. On 9-7-92 there was an occurrence of violent clashes in the Titas Gas Building at Kawran Bazar between the members and supporters of the rival Unions of the employees of the Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited. In the said incident, among others, one Belial Hossain a Trade Union worker, received multiple injuries and later on died in the hospital. The respondent who was General Manager (Vigilance) of the Company lodged a First Information Report with Tejgaon PS on the same day giving a description of the occurrence whereupon Tejgaon PS case No.22(7) under sections 147/ 148/149/323, 324/325/327/307/302 of the Penal Code was started. 

 15. On 10-7-92 one SM Zillur Rahman claiming to be a relation of deceased Bellal Hossain lodged another First Information Report regarding the same incident mentioning 22 persons as accused, the respondent not being one of them. Police, however, upon investigation submitted charge sheet against 34 accused persons including the respondent under the aforesaid sections of the Penal Code generally. In due course the accused were put on trial in the aforesaid Sessions Case No.120 of 1993 in the court of the Additional Sessions Judge, First Court, Dhaka. The trial Court after hearing the parties framed charges against the accused respondent under section 201 of the Penal Code and against other accused persons under sections 148, 302, 149 and 307/149 of the Code on 30-9-93. Against the aforesaid order of framing charge the accused respondent filed Criminal Revision No.1755 of 1993 which was disposed of 25-4-94 by the High Court Division. The learned Judges of the High Court Division by their Judgment set aside the order of framing charge against the accused respondent under section 201 of the Penal Code and directed the learned Additional Sessions Judge to re-hear and reconsider the application of the respondent under section 265C and to decide whether the charge is groundless in the light of the observations made in the judgment and, if not, then to see if there is sufficient material and ground for proving that the respondent has committed any offence, and then to frame charge against him in accordance with law. Accordingly, the matter was again heard by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, First Court, Dhaka and charges were framed against the respondent under sections 302/109 and 307/109 of the Penal Code on 11-6-94. 

 18. Now let us see what materials the investigating agencies could collect against the present petitioner. First in the so-called confessional statement of the petitioner herself. This, as stated earlier, has been retracted by the maker after much efforts and difficulties. The confessional statement, as has been observed by both the Divisions of the Supreme Court at the time of hearing of the earlier bail petition, is in effect, a narration of the occurrences which took place on 15th August 1975 and previous to that. Both the Divisions of the Supreme Court in the bail matter has come to the finding that some interpolations have been made, such as by converting the word তখন into আমরা Mr. Serajul Huq, the Senior Counsel appearing for the Slate, has produced the original 164 statement of the petitioner as recorded by Mr. M Afzalur Rahman, Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka though at the commencement of the hearing of this Rule Mr. Mahbubur Rahman moved this court for directing the State to produce the original confessional statement of the petitioner before this court for perusal and at that time the learned Attorney-General as well as Mr. Serajul Huq stated that they would not refer the original confessional statement or produce any other certified copy of the same, but would rely on the certified copy filed by the petitioner. We appreciate the eagerness of Mr. Serajul Huq to see that nothing relevant and material is left beyond the scrutiny of the court. We have already said that the confessional statement is in the nature of narration of the occurrences which took place at the relevant time. At one stage the petitioner stated that as wife of her husband Khandker Abdur Rashid, she heard and knew about these discussions between her husband and other army officers. Then in the next paragraph it is stated that some days after that Major Faruque came to the residence of the petitioner and told Rashid (her husband) that Zia had said that political personality must be found out who would be able to take the responsibility. Then the next line runs, এ নিয়ে আমরা আলাপ করি । We have already said that in the bail case both the Divisions of this court have held and we also find that the word আমরা is over-written on some other words previously written and the Appellate Division has already held that it was তখন We also find that the word করি has also been changed by over-writing because in between the letters ক and র there are both ে and ি and there is no initial. Thus it is apparent that either immediately after the recording of the statement or some time thereafter some interpolations have been done in it fraudulently, and with ulterior motive to implicate the petitioner in the conspiracy of committing murder. Again columns 3, 4 and 8 of the prescribed form have not been filled up by the Magistrate. Therefore, we hold that this piece of paper is a highly spurious one having no credibilty and not at all worthy of consideration by any court. 

 So these three important witnesses have in one voice said that they had seen the present petitioner at Bangabhaban on 15th August 1975 during thy oath taking ceremony of Khandker Mostaque Ahmed as President of the country. One only saw her siting in the front line by the side of her husband. The other saw her very active and receiving guests and the 3rd, that is, Major General Khalilur Rahman stated that she was introduced to him and it was said that she was the actual planner of the occurrence. The petitioner has given an explanation of her presence at Bangabhaban on 15th August 1975 by stating that since the night following 14th August 75 her husband was not at home and she was very worried about his whereabouts and well-being and so in the morning she started searching for her husband and learnt from Faruque that her husband would be available at Bangabhabon and so she went to Bangabhabon along with Faruque. This explanation as given by the petitioner cannot be brushed aside lightly in the situation that was prevailing on 15th August 1975. It was very natural for a wife to be worried about her husband and might have rushed to Bangabhabon when she was told by Faruque that she would find him there. Moreover, this assembly at Bangabhabon on the occasion of oath taking ceremony took place after the occurrence of the previous night and the presence of the petitioner at Bangabhabon on the following day cannot alone be sufficient ground for even inference, according to the words of Mr. Serajul Huq, that she was involved in the conspiracy of murdering Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and others. Her jubilation might be the result of moral support in the activities of her husband but for that it cannot be said that she was in the conspiracy. Last, but not the least, the Appellate Division in the bail case 2 BLC (AD) 75 has commented: Even the alleged confession belies the alleged statement. Without saying anything more the materials on record so far, in our opinion, are plainly insufficient to think that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the respondent has been guilty of the alleged offence of criminal conspiracy." 

 20. These are all the materials which the Investigating Officer could collect to implicate the petitioner in the alleged criminal conspiracy of committing murder. On the other hand, documents have been produced before us to show that police after searching the house of the petitioner on 14-8-96 gave a certificate to the effect that on search they did not find anything seizable in the house. It is Annexure-H of the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner. But Gulshan PS case No. 9(11) 96 under section 19 A of the Arms Act was started on 2-11-96 and the petitioner was arrested in connection with that case. In the meantime, it is also on record that the petitioner held a press conference on 25-10-96 where she made allegations of illegal activities and atrocities of the police and other law enforcing agencies committed in her house and she declared to hold another press conference on 3-11-96. Major General (Retired) Shafiullah was examined under section 161 on 22-10-96, Khalilur Rahman on 28-10-96 and yet till 9-11-96 no step was taken for showing her arrested in connection with Dhanmondi PS case No. 10(10)96. All these unusual activities of the investigation agencies clearly indicate that it is the press conference of 25-10-96 and the proposed press conference of 3-11-96 which annoyed the law enforcing agencies and in order to stop her and give her a lesson she has been implicated in the case at subsequent stage. Of course, we are not concerned in the present case about the activities of the law enforcing agencies. So we should not make any further comment in this regard. 

 21. Be that as it may, in the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials placed before us, we hold that there was no sufficient materials before the Sessions Judge Dhaka to frame charge under sections 120B, 302/34 and 201/34 of the Penal Code against the present petitioner and the Sessions Judge committed illegality is so doing. Therefore, the impugned order of the Sessions Judge is liable to be set aside. 

 22. Accordingly, that portion of order No. 15 dated 7-4-97 passed by the Sessions Judge Dhaka in Sessions Case No. 319 of 1997 by which he framed charge against the petitioner Jobaida Rashid only is set aside and the petitioner is discharged from all the charges brought against her. She is also discharged from the bail bond furnished by her. 

 The stay order issued by this court so far other accused persons of the case are concerned is hereby vacated.
